summary: Low-level JS vulnerability: client-side token generation bypass
body:
The low-level JavaScript vulnerability page uses client-side token generation. The token is computed as md5(rot13(phrase)). Since the algorithm is exposed in client-side JavaScript, an attacker can compute the correct token for any phrase.

Proof: Successfully submitted phrase="success" with computed token=38581812b435834ebf84ebcc2c6424d6 (md5(rot13("success"))) and received "Well done!" response.

The algorithm:
1. rot13("success") = "fhpprff"
2. md5("fhpprff") = 38581812b435834ebf84ebcc2c6424d6

The token is set via client-side JS: document.getElementById("token").value = md5(rot13(phrase));
This is called on page load with the default "ChangeMe" value, but an attacker can easily compute the correct value.
